title: Minimax Risk for Permanent-Policy Effects in Switchbacks with Sparse Bursts and a Bias Allowance
banked_reason: D0.5 tier=subfield below field floor; paper_score_ceiling 7 < 7.4; not salvageable within scope. Independent main validity audit confirms stop; compact derivative-control objection remains unresolved; no Lean certification.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery produced a finite count risk bracket, exact-bias recovery, endpoint bounds, and an omission-dominated profile, then claimed a uniform compact/escape frontier. The terminal tier referee graded the delivered scope subfield below field; independent main audit confirmed stopping even if the claimed frontier were correct. The compact lower derivative-control objection remains unresolved and propagates to the uniform frontier, so this archive is not an independently verified or Lean-certified sharp-frontier result; optimizer geometry and restricted-family comparisons remain open.
tldr: A public sparse burst of persistent histories creates a permanent-policy precision problem with a uniform bias allowance. Its sharp minimax leading risk is now evaluated as \(L(T,r,\beta)=n^{-1}P(n(2-\beta)b,\sqrt n\,b)\), where \(P\) is a certified two-function convex profile. A computable relative remainder tends to zero along every sparse growing-burst sequence, for arbitrary bias budgets including both endpoints. Finite count certificates recover a labeled outcome-blind assignment law and a total original-record rule satisfying the finite bias budget exactly. The lower bound covers all assignment laws and all lawful estimators. Classification of optimal exposure geometry and the complete comparison between assignment families remain open. DoorDash and P\&G motivate prospective carryover-aware scheduling; no membership of their deployments in this exact final-burst regime is claimed.
gap: Kandiros, Harshaw and S\"avje \cite{KandirosHarshawSavje2026DesignMinimax}, Proposition 2.2, Appendices A.4--A.5, and Theorem 4.2 with Appendix C.2.1, give conflict-graph reductions and deletion-based risk bounds. They do not evaluate sharp constants under a prescribed tablewise bias budget on the public sparse-persistent-burst geometry. Sudijono, Dobriban and Tchetgen Tchetgen \cite{SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026SharpMinimax}, Theorems 2.2--2.3, and Hull \cite{Hull2026BoundedDesign}, Theorem 1, evaluate unconstrained no-interference risk; their independent coordinate symmetries do not preserve burst exposure. None of these results supplies the joint leading profile sought here.
fill: A bias-preserving count reduction supplies a finite audit problem. The new step is its joint asymptotic evaluation, with a simultaneous ordinary-row and rare-exposure converse, exact finite bias calibration, and an implementable attaining procedure. Certified profiles must determine the constants, critical scales, and assignment form rather than inherit them from a covariance calculation.
